summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman was admitted to the psychiatry service after an intentional morphine overdose in the context of severe major depression, chronic abdominal pain from endometriosis, recent breakup, legal issues, and a history of substance misuse. She was transferred from the medical ICU where she was stabilized after presenting with tachycardia and lethargy. During her 9-day psychiatric admission, she engaged fully in treatment, gained insight into her emotional triggers and maladaptive coping mechanisms, and showed marked improvement in mood and pain control. She was tapered off opioids and lorazepam, started on mirtazapine and quetiapine for depression and sleep, and completed a course of antibiotics for an asymptomatic urinary tract infection. Her liver function normalized, and she was discharged home with her mother to begin a partial hospitalization program, with strong motivation for recovery and no suicidal ideation at discharge.
problems: Major depressive affective disorder, single episode, severe, without mention of psychotic behavior
Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Sedative, hypnotic or anxiolytic abuse, continuous
